title: Channel
description: One account this project publishes to: which network, whose account, and what to sign the request with.
guidance: A channel is this project's own — two projects on one machine may publish to the same network under different accounts, which is the whole reason this is a record rather than a setting. Connect it in the section: paste the credential the network asks for — a token, or an app password beside a handle — and the account name and author are read back from the network rather than typed. **The token itself is never here.** `secret` is the name it is kept under in Sync's vault; the value lives in the machine's keychain and does not travel with the repository. The body is what an agent should know about this channel that the fields cannot say — the tone, the audience, who reads it.

network.description: Which network it reaches. Required: a channel is an account somewhere, and one with no network is not a channel yet. The set is closed because a network decides a length limit and a vocabulary of visibility, and a name outside it is a limit nobody can count against. Every name in it can be published to from the window.

account.description: Whose account it is, as the network itself names it. Read back when the channel is connected rather than typed, so it cannot disagree with the token beside it.

author.description: What the network calls the author when it is asked to publish — a person URN on LinkedIn, a DID on Bluesky, a numeric id on Threads and Telegram. Read back on connecting for the same reason `account` is: it is the network's answer, not somebody's recollection.

chat.description: Where inside the network the posts go, for a network that does not decide it from the account. Telegram is the one that does: a bot says nothing anywhere until it is told which chat, and the bot has to be in that chat — an administrator, where it is a channel. Written as it is addressed: `@name` for a channel, a numeric id beginning `-100` for a group. Empty everywhere else, because an account is the whole address there.

secret.description: The name the token is kept under in Sync's vault — never the token. A name is safe to write down and travels usefully: a colleague opening this project sees which secret the channel expects and that their machine has not got it.
